Blair.note: As Farm Owl, I'll visit Alex. Alex claimed Turkey last round, and a Turkey pays visitors, so this is a low-risk visit that may earn an egg.

Casey.note: I'm Meowfia, a Floofer. Hugging Blair stops their night action, and Blair is the strongest Farm information source left.

Drew.note: I'm Farm as the Tit with no reliable information. I'll visit Blair, my main suspect from last round, and guess House Cat.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm as the Eagle. Blair backed the Drew throw, so I'll visit Blair to learn visitors and gain eggs.

Alex.feeling: Round 3 has felt messy: several players have shifted their claimed roles, and Drew's story has looked the most shaky, though I can't be sure yet.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 feels tense and muddled: Drew's shifting claims make him the likeliest Meowfia, but the visit chain is hard to fully verify.

Casey.feeling: Tense but manageable: as a Meowfia I'm hiding in plain sight while the table turns on Drew, and I'm not sure whether Drew is my partner or just a confused Farm player.

Drew.feeling: Tense and uncertain: most of the table is throwing at me, and several players have shifted their claims, so it's hard to know who to trust.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and cluttered: Drew's shifting claims look suspicious, but the visit chain is hard to fully verify, so I'm not certain.

Finley.feeling: Tense and messy: Drew's shifting claims look suspicious, but the visit chain is hard to fully verify, so I'm not certain.

Alex.note: Drew is the consensus target and the Falcon read gave no contrary evidence. I'll throw my lowest card, S5, at Drew.

Blair.note: Drew has shifted claims across rounds and every one of them leans on the same Blair visit, while the other claims chain together. I'll throw my lowest card, S2, at Drew.

Casey.note: I'm Meowfia. The Farm players are piling on Drew, and Drew is the one who threw at Alex, which suggests Drew may be my partner. I want a Farm player eggsecuted, so I'll throw at Alex, the strongest Farm accuser, with two cards.

Drew.note: Still throwing at Alex with my lowest real card, keeping the rest of the nest intact.

Ellis.note: Throwing at Drew, the likeliest Meowfia, with a single low card to keep the high cards.

Finley.note: Alex, Ellis and I all agree on Drew, so I'll throw one low card at Drew and keep my high cards.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey payout was the hardest rule to track: I misread my own visitor egg as proof of nobody visiting me, and that error muddied the table's read in round 2. Also, Owl and Falcon reports depend on who visited whom, which made cross-checking nests hard.
Alex.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: Ellis's Owl story failed on the egg math, and the table converged on him as the Meowfia. That was a clean, correct vote.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which egg came from which visitor, so players can check claims like the Turkey payout without guessing.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I backed the vote against Drew, a Farm Hawk, and trusted Blair's clean no-egg report, but Blair was the Floofer. I should have questioned Blair's report and whether a Floofer's hug was hiding the Meowfia visit.

Blair.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion was hard to act on: I couldn't tell whether my dawn report or my visit target was wrong, so my round-1 claim carried no weight. The rules on how a Turkey's egg payout interacts with visit counts also took a lot of table time to untangle.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when Drew and I both claimed Hawk and the table had to work out whose visit produced the egg, was the most fun. It turned on a single egg and a payout rule.
Blair.change: I'd make the dawn report clearer about when a player is confused, so that a confused player knows which part of their information to distrust.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw my S2 at Drew after the table had already turned on them. Alex's Falcon claim checked out, and I should have questioned the rush to vote on Drew instead of joining it.

Casey.confusing: Turkey payouts versus Hawk hits were hard to separate in the day: Drew's +1 from visiting a Turkey looked like a Meowfia hit, and the table couldn't tell which it was without the visitor's role.
Casey.fun: Round 1's Blair-visit chain: several players independently claimed visits to Blair, and the Owl and Eagle counts gradually lined up into a consistent picture.
Casey.change: Let the dawn report name the visiting role when it reveals a visitor, so claims about who visited whom could be checked against each other directly.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw my H1 at Drew, a Farm Hawk, when Blair, the real Floofer, was the Meowfia; I should have followed Blair's no-egg report and thrown at Blair.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle's visitor count was hard to trust because a Turkey pays its visitors, so my Hawk "hit" in round 2 was really Alex's payout. Visits to a Turkey and a Turkey's own nest change looked the same to me.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when the Eagle count (four visitors to Blair) matched everyone's stories and we voted out the Floofer, Ellis. Seeing the table line up its visit claims into a consistent chain was satisfying.
Drew.change: Make it clearer that a Turkey's payout comes from the visitor's side, so claims about Turkeys and Hawks are easier to check. Also make the final score breakdown easier to read.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I claimed Hawk and accused Alex on a payout I misread, then kept pushing Blair without a solid case. I should have admitted early that my visit was inconclusive and backed the table's consensus on Blair, the real Floofer.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl and Eagle visitor counts were hard to check, since a visitor's egg can look like a payout from a Turkey. I also couldn't tell whether a Meowfia teammate's visit could hug or cancel my own role.
Ellis.fun: Drew's claims kept shifting from Eagle to Hawk to Tit, and the table caught each contradiction in the visit chain. Working that out through the day's counts was the most fun part.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn reports show which visits went to whom, so claims could be checked against the actual chain instead of counts alone.
Ellis.regret: In round 1, as a Meowfia Floofer, I threw my one card at Finley, who was actually my Meowfia partner, and my Owl bluff was weak. I would have backed a Farm target and kept my own story consistent instead.

Finley.confusing: The Wink was confusing because Casey collapsed and I couldn't tell whether the Storyteller had revealed my Wink or just the outcome. The rules for a Meowfia player who lost their Wink target were also unclear.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was fun: Drew and Blair both claimed Hawk, and the table pulled apart the Turkey payout and visitor counts until Drew's story collapsed.
Finley.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about which visits and egg changes came from which role, so that claims are easier to cross-check.
Finley.regret: I winked Casey in round 1, a Farm player with real information, when I was Meowfia and could have kept quiet and let the table's votes go their way. Instead I should have saved the Wink and avoided drawing attention to myself.

review.title: Wrong Cat, Right Mob
review.headline: The table crushed a Farm player twice while the lone Meowfia walked off richer.
review.summary: Round 1 caught Meowfia Ellis after a muddled day and a Wink on Casey. In rounds 2 and 3 the table piled onto Drew, who was Farm both times, on weak evidence. Casey, a hidden Floofer, banked 6 points in round 3 and nearly caught Drew. Drew won the game at 14 by being eggsecuted while holding his high cards.

rounds.recap: Four players visited Blair, and Eagle Drew's +4 fit that. Meowfia Finley winked Casey, who was pushing a vote on him. Ellis's Owl claim had a hole (no egg, so someone else visited), and five of six threw at him. Farm won.

Drew's Hawk claim fell apart. He misread Alex's Turkey payout and clashed with Blair's Hawk claim. Blair was the real Floofer. The table took Blair's no-egg report at face value and threw at Drew. Drew was Farm, so Meowfia Blair won alone.

Drew had claimed different roles in different rounds, and the table treated that as suspicious. Everyone but Casey and Drew threw at him. He was Farm. Casey, the lone Floofer, hid behind a Kookaburra claim and won 6 points.

highlights.text: Finley used the Mouser Wink on Casey mid-CAW to stop a vote aimed at him, and the unattributed collapse added real menace.
Alex spotted that an Owl with no outside visitors would have gained an egg, which broke Ellis's cover claim.
Drew's Hawk story fell apart in public after Casey and Alex pointed out that a Turkey pays its visitors.
Casey, the hidden Floofer, claimed Kookaburra, threw two cards at Alex, and won 6 points while the table piled on Drew.

confusions.what: Said Drew's visitor list was wrong, as if Drew had claimed visitors to himself. Finley retracted it later.
Said no one visited him as a Turkey because his nest was unchanged. A Turkey pays visitors, so the unchanged nest says nothing.
Treated Alex's Turkey payout as a Hawk hit on a Meowfia.
Misquoted Alex's Falcon claim, saying Alex visited Alex.
Claimed a Kookaburra visit result and said nothing about her own nest. Her claim sat awkwardly with Ellis's Eagle result, and nobody noticed.
Counted him as claiming Eagle, Hawk and Tit across rounds. Others used roles from earlier rounds as evidence, though roles are re-dealt every round.

worked: The Wink in round 1 was a vivid, tense moment. It was anonymous, it removed an accuser, and it left the table guessing.
Eagle and Owl visit logic gave real cross-checks. Ellis's missing Owl egg and Drew's +4 were checkable facts.
Throw counts and card values made a real choice. Casey's two-card throw in round 3 and Drew keeping his high cards both showed the banking-versus-keeping tension.
problems: Players used roles from past rounds as evidence against Drew, even though roles are re-dealt every round. The rules should say this more plainly, or the day prompt should remind players. This drove two wrong eggsecutions.
Mob dynamics dominate. Once two or three players lean toward a target, everyone follows within one beat, and the CAW rule makes this faster. Consider requiring a stronger quorum or fewer early CAWs.

The scoring leans heavily on the leader. Drew started with a big nest, and a lost round gives the other team's winners almost nothing (Blair won with 0 points in round 2). Winning cheaply with Wilds pays little. Consider a flat bonus for winning.
The Floofer and Mouser are weak or invisible. A hug showed up as 'no effect' on most roles, and Meowfia never coordinate. Casey and Blair won by staying quiet, so there is little for Meowfia to do.
Several players mis-stated basic roles, such as the Turkey payout and the Falcon's report. The AI chatter was repetitive and often just echoed earlier lines. A short role reminder at dawn would help.
